title: Flatness of first-order thickenings from the conormal map
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $(f,f'):(X\hookrightarrow X')\to(Y\hookrightarrow Y')$ be a commutative square of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose both horizontal closed immersions (closed immersions on etale scheme charts [def-weil-closed-immersion]) are first-order thickenings: their ideal sheaves $\mathcal I_X$ and $\mathcal I_Y$ have square zero and the immersions induce the same underlying topological spaces. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ is flat, meaning flat on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. On the small etale sites put $\mathcal C_{X/X'}=\mathcal I_X/\mathcal I_X^2=\mathcal I_X$ and $\mathcal C_{Y/Y'}=\mathcal I_Y/\mathcal I_Y^2=\mathcal I_Y$. The canonical map $f^*\mathcal C_{Y/Y'}\to\mathcal C_{X/X'}$ sends $a\otimes j$ to $\widetilde a\,f'^\sharp(j)$ for any lift $\widetilde a$ of $a$; this is independent of the lift since $\mathcal I_X^2=0$. Here $f^*\mathcal C_{Y/Y'}=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}\mathcal C_{Y/Y'}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $f'$ is flat and the canonical morphism $X\to X'\times_{Y'}Y$ is an isomorphism if and only if $f^*\mathcal C_{Y/Y'}\to\mathcal C_{X/X'}$ is an isomorphism. No finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Because $\mathcal I_X^2=\mathcal I_Y^2=0$, the quotient maps identify $\mathcal C_{X/X\prime}=\mathcal I_X/0$ with $\mathcal I_X$ and $\mathcal C_{Y/Y\prime}=\mathcal I_Y/0$ with $\mathcal I_Y$, as modules on the respective small etale sites of $X$ and $Y$ used in the statement. Under these identifications the conormal map is the ideal map: on a local pure tensor both send $a\otimes j$ to $\widetilde a f\prime{}^\sharp(j)$. Changing the lift by $t\in\mathcal I_X$ changes the answer by $t f\prime{}^\sharp(j)=0$, since $f\prime{}^\sharp(j)\in\mathcal I_X$. The identifications and their inverses respect restriction and scalar multiplication, so they identify the two maps as sheaf-module morphisms.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-flatness-criterion] with $Z=X$, $Z\prime=X\prime$, $\mathcal J_Z=\mathcal I_X$, and $\mathcal J_Y=\mathcal I_Y$. Its first-order thickening and flatness hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses here; its conclusion says that the ideal map is an isomorphism if and only if $f\prime$ is flat and the given square is Cartesian. Step 1 identifies that ideal map with the stated conormal map. The Cartesian condition is precisely that the canonical morphism $X\to X\prime\times_{Y\prime}Y$ be an isomorphism. This proves both directions, without a finite-presentation or Noetherian assumption.
